A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PowerCLIP research work, including Appendices A–H. Text and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison of the methods, equations, results and visual material.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification, retrieval, robustness and compositionality experiments, ablations, computational measurements and appendix OV-COCO results.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–15 and the empirical analyses and visualizations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain identical region and phrase embeddings, powerset alignment, triplet objectives, NLA-T1/T2 approximations and PowerCLIP-R/S variants.

E1.justification: CC12M training and all classification, retrieval, robustness, compositionality and linear-probing evaluations are unchanged. The synthetic approximation tests and appendix OV-COCO evaluation are also retained.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain CLIP, FLIP, A-CLIP, E-CLIP, C-PGS, FILIP and SPARC. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the Winoground, computational-cost, OV-COCO and qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same architectures, preprocessing, training budget, batch size and evaluation metrics. The appendix matched-compute comparison, mask-scaling tests and other experimental procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component, mask, activation and hyperparameter ablations, robustness evaluations, approximation checks, computational analyses and qualitative examples. Correcting the qualitative-examples heading does not change the analysis.

E5.justification: The Pearson-correlation analysis and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–15 and the plotted and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, both report PowerCLIP-S average classification accuracy of 42.2%, average retrieval R@1 of 47.0%, and PowerCLIP OV-COCO AP50 of 24.4.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, approximation theorems, corollary and derivations are identical, including the complete proofs of Theorems 1 and 2 in Appendices A–B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same powerset-alignment contribution, exponential-to-linear approximation claim, and performance, compositionality and robustness claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of compositional grounding, approximation accuracy, mask robustness and computational overhead are unchanged. No substantive applicability qualification or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces v3's promise that code will become public with a statement that code is available and a GitHub address for Masakichi210/PowerCLIP. Other implementation details are unchanged; the PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the positioning relative to visual masking, textual augmentation and multimodal alignment methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 5.3 corrects the heading 'Quantitative Examples' to 'Qualitative Examples.' The abstract updates its code-availability sentence, while the narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer code notice produces limited text reflow on pages 1–2, and the corrected heading slightly changes wrapping on page 8. Figures, tables, captions and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves reproducibility guidance by supplying a concrete code repository address instead of promising a future release, and improves clarity by correcting the qualitative-examples heading. The scientific evidence and appendices are unchanged. This assessment concerns the documented access information, without assuming that repository contents have been verified.
